text:
incident-bot: ALERT — kv-cache: continuous-batching error-rate spike detected in us-west-2. kv-evict-rate > 300/s, overall errors > 2.8% over 5m

alex: paging oncall. observing sudden p95 jumps and a cluster of paging events originating from a handful of heavy tenants. dashboards: https://redwood.internal/ops/kv-cache?range=10m

sam: ack. grabbing traces/eviction logs now. which tenants are the biggest offenders?

maria: hot tenants: tenant-99 (30% of QPS), tenant-alpha (12%), tenant-7 (4%). tenant-99 miss-rate up 3% -> 55% in 12m. looks like prefix aggregation + larger batch_window_v2 ramped this morning.

josh: theory: new batch-window-v2 heuristics are overaggregating streams, creating cache hotset churn for tenants with many low-fanout prefixes. result = eviction amplification + paging loops.

sam: immediate mitigation plan: 1) create per-tenant overrides for top offenders to pin batching.size and batch_window to conservative defaults; 2) enable per-shard prewarm for tenant shards that see cold-cache spikes; 3) run a controlled canary for smaller batch_window across 7% traffic, monitor 15m windows.

ops-bot: queued feature operation: feature-flip batch-window-v2 -> partial-rollout mode

sam: applying quick override for tenant-99 to set batching.size=6 and batch_window_ms=50 for 20m. running command:
```
curl -s -X POST "https://flags.redwood/api/v1/overrides" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"tenant":"tenant-99","flag":"batch-window-v2","batching.size":6,"batch_window_ms":50,"ttl":"20m"}'
```

incident-bot: ACTION — override created for tenant-99 (ttl=20m)

maria: after override tenant-99 p95 down from 2.1s -> 200ms within 3m, global error-rate down to 0.8%

alex: nice. we should avoid a global flip. suggest cohort rollout: cohort A = top-10 tenants per-QPS (immediate overrides), cohort B = 7% randomized canary rollout (batch-window-v2 reduced), cohort C = gradual ramp to 25% if stable. fallback: auto-rollback if any tenant p95 > 1s for >4m or global error_rate > 1.5%

josh: I'll prep automation to create per-tenant overrides. who runs the canary?

sam: I'll kick canary. naming slice "bw2-split-2026-03-15". steps: create overrides for top-10 then enable canary 7% traffic. monitor kv-evict-rate, miss-rate, and p95 for 10m windows.

ops-bot: automation started: creating per-tenant overrides (10/10)

ops-bot: log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-15T15:02:11Z] override created tenant-99 batching.size=6
[2026-03-15T15:02:12Z] override created tenant-alpha batching.size=6
[2026-03-15T15:02:13Z] override created tenant-7 batching.size=6
... (others)
```

maria: metrics update: overall p95 down to 230ms, kv-evict-rate halved. ready to enable canary at 7%

sam: enabling canary: POST /api/v1/flags/batch-window-v2/canary { "slice":"bw2-split-2026-03-15", "percent":7 }

incident-bot: CANARY ENABLED — 7%

jules: watching canary dashboard: https://redwood.internal/observability/canaries/bw2-split-2026-03-15. first 12m look clean.

maria: after 12m the canary is stable. propose bump to 15%, watch 15m.

sam: bump to 15% now. remember to watch mid-tier tenants for cold-cache-induced p95 bumps.

incident-bot: CANARY UPDATED — 15%

josh: at +8m post-bump we see tenant-33 p95 jump 220ms -> 750ms but error-rate stayed low. likely prewarm needed. applying prewarm job for shard-5.

maria: prewarm kicked: shard-5 prewarm job started (targeted key prefixes warmed)

customer-success: alerting the top affected accounts with a short note: "We've applied mitigations for intermittent latency; no requests lost. We'll share a post-incident summary." tagging customer teams for tenant-99 and tenant-alpha.

anya: i'm taking the handoff at 18:00 UTC. will monitor the ramp and keep rollback path ready. adding a watch script to auto-trigger rollback if thresholds exceed.

alex: explicit rollback criteria: 1) any tenant p95 > 1s for >4m, 2) global error_rate > 1.5% for 5m, or 3) kv-evict-rate > 200/s sustained for 6m -> run emergency-rollback which sets batching.size back to 1 and disables batch-window-v2 globally.

sam: rollback command documented:
```
POST /api/v1/flags/batch-window-v2/rollback
{ "reason":"kv_eviction_amp","apply_globally":true }
```

ops-bot: emergency-rollback playbook: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/kv-batch-rollback

josh: will own the postmortem and follow-ups. initial action items: 1) revert batch-window-v2 default to conservative heuristics; 2) add per-shard eviction telemetry and alerting; 3) add regression test in perf-harness simulating skewed prefix access.

maria: also recommend: add dynamic per-tenant autosuppress that throttles batching heuristics when eviction/sec thresholds exceeded, and expose safer defaults behind rollout gates.

sam: incident RESOLVED — metrics stable for 40m, canary at 15% but top-10 have overrides in place. scheduling follow-up meeting to land long-term fixes.

customer-success: sending wrap-up to impacted customers and opening support cases for BigCorp (SR-4219) and FinPartner (SR-4220).

alex: closing notes: thread kept as canonical incident log. josh will post the formal postmortem in #postmortems within 24h. please drop raw captures and pcap-style dumps into #incidents-archive if you have them. thanks all.
